mappings.note: What संदेश the poem gives -- the powerful cannot silence the people for long. A response to the poem's message on सत्ता के अंत, so C-H2.1-LO-8 rather than LO-4.
What the 1857 cannon was used for (to crush the revolt). Historical fact recalled from the poem, LO-4 and not C-H2.1-LO-8.
What the cannon used to be used for (killing Indian revolutionaries). Content recall, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.

Why the cannon's mouth is eventually shut -- because force is never the final answer. The poem's message about the end of power, hence C-H2.1-LO-8; C-H2.1-LO-7 is reserved for items that read the birds on the cannon as the symbol.
Why the British army used the cannon (to suppress patriots). A repeat recall item, mapped LO-4 as before.
What सीख the cannon gives. A response to the poem's message, so C-H2.1-LO-8 rather than plain content recall under LO-4.
Which collection won the prize ('इसी दुनिया'). Literary-award fact, so C-H2.3. Repeat of the earlier item whose stem wrongly names श्रीकांत वर्मा -- the same defect, reported.
What the 1857 cannon was used for -- duplicate stem, mapped LO-4 like its twin.

What the sparrow tells us by getting inside the cannon -- pride is broken, every power ends. That is exactly what the birds on the dead cannon symbolise, so C-H2.1-LO-7 rather than LO-6's gossip scene.
When the cannon would have been used (1857). Factual recall, LO-4 and not LO-5.

Meaning of the मुहावरा 'धज्जियाँ उड़ाना' asked in general. Idiom knowledge is a व्याकरण item, so C-H2.2 -- unlike the sibling item that asks the लाक्षणिक sense of 'मुँह बंद होना' inside the poem, which is LO-5.
What the cannon says to the सैलानी (that it is deadly and powerful). Content of the speaking-cannon passage, so LO-4.
What the cannon serves for now (the boys' riding). Recall about the children, not the birds, so LO-4 rather than C-H2.1-LO-6.
Who gossips sitting on the cannon (the birds). The गपशप प्रसंग that C-H2.1-LO-6 names, so that outcome rather than generic LO-4.
What सीख you take from the cannon -- time is stronger than power. An expressed reaction to the poem's message, so C-H2.1-LO-8 and not LO-4.
What the poet means by 'अच्छे-अच्छे सूरमाओं के धज्जे'. Construing the phrase's bitterness is भाव-पक्ष, so LO-5; the general idiom item is C-H2.2 instead.

What लाक्षणिक sense 'मुँह बंद होना' carries in this poem. The question is about the figure's working inside the text, so LO-5 -- not C-H2.2, which would be right only for the idiom asked in the abstract.
Why inherited things are preserved, and to what purpose. The धरोहरों के संरक्षण strand of C-H2.1-LO-8 rather than LO-4's factual recall.
Which kind of छंद the poem uses (मुक्त छंद). Verse form is the कला-पक्ष, so LO-5; C-H2.2 covers grammar, not prosody.
Meaning of 'सूरमा' (= वीर). A शब्दार्थ gloss on the poem's diction, so LO-5 rather than C-H2.2.
Viren Dangwal's date and place of birth. कवि-परिचय, so the literature competency rather than any poem-bound outcome.
Why the cannon calls itself 'जबर' -- because it destroyed many revolutionaries in 1857. A reason the poem states, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
How many of Dangwal's collections have appeared. Bibliographic fact, hence C-H2.3.
Where the 1857 cannon is kept (the Company Bagh entrance). Factual recall, LO-4; the 'why is it kept there' items are C-H2.1-LO-8.
From whom the cannon came to us (the British, as विरासत). A fact, so LO-4 rather than C-H2.1-LO-8.
Explain the आशय of 'उड़ा दिए थे मैंने अच्छे-अच्छे सूरमाओं के धज्जे'. Quoted-line construal, so LO-5 and not LO-4.
What संदेश the poem gives -- even the mightiest must end. The poem's message on सत्ता के अंत, so C-H2.1-LO-8 rather than LO-5's theme-statement items.
On which two dates the cannon is polished (15 August, 26 January). Factual recall, LO-4 and not C-H2.1-LO-8.
How many times a year the cannon is polished (twice). Plain fact, so LO-4.
Who gets inside the cannon in mischief (the गौरैया). The sparrow passage that C-H2.1-LO-6 names, so that outcome rather than LO-4.
Why the 1857 cannon is still kept in the Company Bagh -- it has become a cultural धरोहर that keeps the past before us. Heritage conservation, so C-H2.1-LO-8 and not LO-4.
The प्रतिपाद्य of 'तोप'. Stating the poem's central burden is भाव-पक्ष व्याख्या, so LO-5; C-H2.1-LO-8 is kept for items that ask for a सीख or a reaction rather than a statement of theme.
Write the poem's संदेश in your own words -- never misuse power, fear no aggressor. That is the reaction C-H2.1-LO-8 describes, unlike the प्रतिपाद्य items mapped LO-5.
What सीख the cannon gives, to be made clear from the poem -- tyrannical power always ends. C-H2.1-LO-8 rather than LO-4.
Make the प्रतिपाद्य of 'तोप' clear. A statement of the poem's theme, so LO-5, matching the other प्रतिपाद्य item and distinct from the संदेश items under C-H2.1-LO-8.
What you know about the Company Bagh -- the gardens the East India Company laid out. Contextual fact behind the poem, so LO-4 rather than C-H2.1-LO-8.
The आशय of '1857 की तोप'. Construing the title phrase and what it evokes is भाव-पक्ष, so LO-5; the plain 'which war' item is LO-4.
What the birds' chirping on the cannon reveals. This is precisely the symbol C-H2.1-LO-7 names -- the once-terrifying weapon reduced to a perch -- rather than LO-6's gossip content.
How the cannon introduces itself. The answer is the enumerated facts of the poem, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
What the सैलानी learn about the cannon. Content of the poem assembled, hence LO-4 and not C-H2.1-LO-8.
The cannon's present condition and why its रौब-दाब is gone. The answer describes the state the poem shows, so LO-4; the items that draw a सीख from that state are C-H2.1-LO-8.
How many kinds of प्रतीक and धरोहर there are and what use they serve. A reflection on heritage and what it teaches, squarely C-H2.1-LO-8 rather than LO-4.
The cannon frightens by its size, yet children and birds play on it -- what is the poet proving? The deliverable is the symbolism of that play, so C-H2.1-LO-7 rather than LO-6 or LO-8.
Why inherited things are preserved and what सीख the cannon gives. Both halves are the heritage/end-of-power message, so C-H2.1-LO-8 rather than LO-4.
Why inherited things are carefully preserved, from 'तोप'. Heritage conservation, C-H2.1-LO-8 and not LO-4.
Same heritage-preservation prompt without the poem named; still the धरोहरों के संरक्षण response, so C-H2.1-LO-8.
Why inherited things matter, on the basis of 'तोप'. A reasoned response on heritage, hence C-H2.1-LO-8 rather than the factual LO-4.
